story.endgame_shedu.dlg.speech_3:
At first I thought the severing of Gannix from physical reality, and the vast fires devouring the surface of Venus, would be sacrifice enough. But Gagtungr waited.

So long as AnCom's sorcerers existed, the appearance was delayed. They were wretched things, yet they were still guardians of the final door. Arrogant creatures. They thought the abyss could be measured with a ruler, that the duration of fate could be assessed by clocks, that a barrier could be set between birth and that which must be born. They were wrong in almost everything, but not in everything. While their Rite still breathed, while they stood between Earth and the thing that comes, the path was not yet cleared.

We cleared it. You brought me beneath the shell of the Silver Sphere, and from within I caused it to burst. That energy was enough for Gagtungr to appear from the power of Olirna upon the Red and Gold Throne. I see his contours emerging. I already see his presence. It was impossible to describe even then, when I was a god, let alone now.
story.endgame_shedu.dlg.speech_4:
Gagtungr is the one before whom my rebellion and my service mean the same thing. My war, Tezctlan's empire, the fear of the live-born, the works of the secret Order, and the cold of Olirna—these were not parts of a struggle, but preparations for an appearance. We thought we were returning to the foot of the Throne. In truth, we were only the soil beneath it.

That is why I no longer call myself a god. It is a title that has lost its meaning. Gagtungr does not come for a title. He comes in such a manner that, after him, titles turn to trash.

In a few minutes, together, we shall behold a being before whom gods, rebels, emperors, and saviors alike will lose the right even to their names.
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.question_1: Gagtungr said that both of you have to be killed. Urparp is the seed of destruction. You are the seed of life. What does that mean?
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.question_2: You speak of yourself as a god. But you were a quasimorph. What are hylonauts, really?
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.question_3: Who is Gagtungr? The one who will inherit the Empire you created?
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.speech_1:
Wait, priest. The obsidian knife is in your hands. Do you not remember where it came from? The moment Gagtungr showed you his face, your hand on the command bridge of the Magnum felt its warm hilt. Now that the Red and Gold Throne has shown you the face of its master, there is no more need for obscure prophecies.

Only the trigger mechanism remains, and it is already in your hands. Like it or not, Gagtungr will have everything to appear in the world in full. Olirna has already given the energy to the Sun, and humanity has already built what is ready to receive it.

I myself created the priest capable of making the sacrifice when the god lies on the altar.
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.speech_2:
Urparp was always destruction, even when he tried to build a kingdom.

Once, long before your ascent into space, the understanding descended upon all bramfaturas that Gagtungr would not emerge from the Great Fire. The Red and Gold Throne would remain empty. At that moment, Urparp began trying the throne on for himself.

He raised Ur in war against the other bramfaturas. He wanted not to serve, but to rule. For this, Fokerma and I cast him down. I plunged Itzpapalotl into his armor, getting to the living core. At that same moment, he grew heavy with matter and fell into your world. There he waited among the red dust until his rage itself became part of a larger design.

I served Gagtungr, and I considered Urparp's uprising an absolute disobedience. In a moment of clarity, I thought I understood my enemy's mistake. Having been on Earth, having satiated myself on your emotions, your way of thinking, your uncontrollable desires, I realized what I wanted. Returning to Venus, I realized that Urparp had been wrong in building a kingdom in the world of the bramfaturas. The true empire had to be created in your world. There is someone to rule here, and someone to serve.

Urparp wanted to subjugate everything to destruction. I wanted to subjugate everything to life and blood. I hoped for the marriage of two worlds. That is why Gagtungr called me the seed of life.

I sent you to take the Itzpapalotl to Urparp so that I could personally appear through him. I wanted to kill Urparp because I thought that if the seed of destruction was destroyed, Gagtungr would lack the final component for his birth. I was wrong. Urparp died, and I survived for the sacrifice. The god himself came to his own altar.
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.speech_3:
Hylonauts. How beautiful your language of science is. Those sailing through matter. Those who left their bramfaturas and passed beyond the shell of the Silver Sphere.

Not every quasimorph could become a hylonaut. There is little gavvakh inside the bramfaturas. There is hierarchy, intrigue, a sense of rank, and lots of emotions. But we always had too little food for the great crossing. To break through to Earth, one had to be more than just strong. One had to stand so high that someone else's suffering flowed to you for millennia.

When we penetrated beyond the thin shell, we clothed ourselves in matter. We entered into stone or gold, the weaker of us into the wood or bones of humans and animals. Religion was not mankind's mistake. All your beliefs were our way of being present on Earth. Every sacrifice was our food. People thought they were feeding gods. In this, they were almost right for once.

But we did not just feed on your fears, we changed you and the world around you. Every great hylonaut brought the landscape, language, and essence of his bramfatura to Earth. Someone taught people the iron discipline of a dungeon, someone forced them to build temples in the midst of deserts, and someone whispered poems from the dark thickets of relict forests. The Earth, which you consider your natural history, is written exclusively in our dreams.

I brought Gannix to your Earth. You call it the bloodthirstiness of the New World. I call it my first empire. Had it not been for the Spaniards, who wiped out everyone who knew how to properly serve me a cup of gavvakh, I would have ruled to this day. But I had to sleep, too. When I woke up, I was already on Venus, and before me stood an enthusiastic worshiper. I had to bless him with instantaneous decapitation. It seems there was so much life energy in me that he didn't die. An amusing side effect.

Now my life is in your hands. Cut out my heart, and Gagtungr will come.
story.endgame_tezctlan.dlg.speech_4:
Empire? You still imagine a pyramid where a lord must necessarily be at the top. I thought so too. But first, look at your hands. You already have the obsidian knife. It does not require your consent. Cut my heart out carefully. Raise it high. Come here. I want to illuminate this world for the last time, a moment before all the lights go out when he appears.

My life and Urparp's war, your victories, Xiomara and her feminine pride—all of this did not contradict itself. All this worked toward the appearance of Gagtungr. It is impossible to squeeze him inside even the widest empire.

Gagtungr is life and destruction, empire and rebellion, freedom and slavery, god and sacrifice all at the same time. He is all-unity and necessity. The principle of causality that, in passing, is capable of creating an entire universe serving only one private goal—his appearance.
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.question_2: Are you saying Tezctlan was a threat not to humans, but to quasimorphs?
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.question_3: So you won? Who is Gagtungr? Your child? A new god? The last ruler?
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.speech_1:
Was it good for you, darling? I do not mean pleasure. It is too late to pretend that what happened between us was something so small. The end of the world is only minutes away. Tezctlan is dead. The Emerald Empire is broken, and the Nakals can no longer put it back together. Gannix has returned to its borders.

And while you thought you were receiving your reward for this victory, I gave you the very thing for which this whole war was fought. You did not notice, but it is already inside you. The spider's egg is already stirring within you. From it, Gagtungr is destined to be born, and I am to become the greatest mother. Many could have received this role, but I alone was able to take it. And if I am to be honest with you, I must confess: I was pleased that you came willingly.
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.speech_2:
What I promised. I freed Venus and Gannix from Tezctlan. I tore away his imperial mask. I restored the taltnoms to their true role in the Solar System. We were never a toy in the hands of some sovereign who wished to create a faction to wage war on humans in the physical world. And on your terms, no less. Tezctlan spent too long on Earth. Your emotions soaked too deeply into him—emotions he drank in with the gavvakh when blood flowed to him from the summits of the great pyramids.

The true role of the taltnoms does not lie in bodiless fantasies that humans might give us something new. Our true role—the role of every bramfatura—was only to let Gagtungr come into the world. We fought only over who would be first. On that path, I was forced to wake Urparp. I was afraid he would manage to use your zeal before I did. Fortunately, you chose correctly.

You are looking for solid ground now. You are thinking that I deceived you. There is no lie here. I never said I served humanity. I never called you the savior of mankind. I never promised you a place at my future court. Those are all your words. You carry them with you like dirt on your soles. I spoke of Tezctlan. Only of him.

He violated an order older than your states and corporations. Yes, much is permitted to the taltnoms. We may pass through flesh, drink gavvakh, love, hate, or wage war. One thing is not permitted. A taltnom must not confuse service with dominance. Tezctlan confused them. That is why he had to die.

And you were obedient enough, and stubborn enough, to bring us to this place. Itzpapalotl was not my gift to you. Nanahuatzin, Topiltzin, and Tonatiuh were not merely trials meant to prove you worthy of touching me. With your help, I was taking the locks off the gates of the Feathered Temple.
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.speech_3:
Of course. Do you think every great crime is committed against you? You are an accident on the underside of the true world. Humans suffered because of Tezctlan, but he had to disappear not because he hurt humans. Human pain is a river, and it is a delight to swim in it. His guilt was not in your blood, but in his theft of the birthright.

He, like Urparp once before him, believed too deeply in the male architecture of power. Upward, higher, toward the throne, toward force, toward command. He saw the bramfatura granted to him as merely a kingdom. He saw the taltnoms not as kin, but as retinue, and humans not as the warm flesh of the world, but as the population of a future empire.

But beneath the vulgar surface of male war, there was another path to Gagtungr's appearance. Fokerma listened to the hum of Olirna in the silence of the Moon. Fukabirna stoked her fires to rival the Sun. Many sisters could have become the mother. But I became her. Because I acted. I thought of the Feathered Masks as my children. I lured you with femininity. Even Jane, commander of your clones, inspired me.

Sisters may betray and envy one another, but we know something men were not made to understand. Greatness need not come from outside. It may be born from within—from the womb. Your body will serve nicely for that. Eccolapse and live birth at once.
story.endgame_xiomara.dlg.speech_4:
I won, and you are still trying to clutch at the old world with words...

Gagtungr is not my child in the sense in which your children belong to their mothers. Motherhood is not property, but participation in transformation. The oldest and darkest participation of all. He is not a new god. Even the cruelest gods are at least somehow bound to those they torment or exalt. Gagtungr is greater than that. He used the gods themselves in order to be born. He is not the last ruler. Do you really think the end of the world needs someone to govern it?

With Gagtungr's appearance, everything that existed and had been named before loses its meaning. Gagtungr is the one before whose birth the very dispute over who was master becomes ridiculous.

Now he will begin to come out. Try not to scream for too long, darling. Too much noise is bad for newborns.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.after: AnCom has cut off all contact with the Solar System. Its SBN addresses still respond at the network level, but queries come back with a different signature structure. It is as if someone took AnCom and the Civil Resistance and combined them into a single megastructure. This may have been their fallback plan all along—to go into full lockdown. But something tells me that very strange things are about to start happening in the Solar System.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.briefing:
The facility's layout is simple. I’ll walk you through it. Four floors. The Fourth Level is locked. That's where the Hellstrom Network computer is located.

Look for Issachar's three key colnodes on the first three floors. Each of them should have a Red Chip. Your job is to collect the chips.

While you do that, we’ll figure out how to get you access upstairs. Don't get distracted from the objective unless it's absolutely unavoidable. There's already enough madness in the world.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.desc: <color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Find three Red Chips and install them into the central computer.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.details:
Details: The Civil Resistance is torn by internal conflict. Several factions are vying for control of the movement, and one of its most dangerous commanders, Issachar, has taken charge of planning operations in the Inner System. To coordinate the colnodes connected to his Hellstrom Network, he is building a special computer system. AnCom has not disclosed the technical details to us. Right now, this system is being integrated at the Civil Resistance base near the Humankind's Hope Citadel Station. AnCom believes this is the best—and possibly the last—window for a strike. You need to find three Red Chips inside the base. According to the client, they are held by key colnodes responsible for the final activation of the Network. Eliminate the colnodes, take the chips, and install them into the coordinating computer. After that, AnCom will intercept the control signal and gain access to the Hellstrom Network.

Additional: It does not look like AnCom intends to destroy Issachar or finish off the Civil Resistance in the usual way. Most likely, they know enough about Dr. Hellstrom's technology to try taking control of the Network rather than destroying it. If they succeed, we will be looking at the largest hacking attack in human history. There is one more detail: AnCom seems to have infiltrated these enemies of the people a very long time ago. The data transmitted to us for this contract is marked with the codename "Justas". Judging by the archive footprints, this is an agent who has been operating inside the Civil Resistance for a long time. Possibly the same person the Resistance has previously used in operations against AnCom itself. If so, the client didn't just find a weak point. AnCom has been embedded in the Resistance for years.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_1: Our satellite has reached its calculated orbit around <color=#FFFEC1>Pallas</color>. The channel is stable. We are personally stepping in to coordinate the operation. Continue the sweep. From this moment on, we can see the facility's layout almost as well as the colnode network itself does.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_10: You are in immediate proximity to the control computer of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. We can confirm that <color=#FFFEC1>Issachar</color> was preparing a large-scale integration of the computer system and his own distributed consciousness here. Proceed strictly according to protocol from here on out. Install the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color> into the computer and await instructions.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_11: This is it. Install the three <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color> into the receiver slots, and our part of the operation will begin. Don't wander off. Biosignatures around the base are on the move. It is possible Issachar prepared reserves for a counterattack.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_12: We have gained access to the control settings of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. Beginning two-way integration. <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> structures will be embedded into the <color=#FFFEC1>Civil Resistance</color> and Civil Resistance structures will be embedded into AnCom. Operation <color=#FFFEC1>Hive Awakening</color> has begun. Hold your position. All biosignatures on the base are heading your way. Evacuation is forbidden until integration is complete. You must survive while we become one.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_13: Integration continues. The satellite has detected another counterattack wave. The good news is that this is a residual reaction from Issachar's structure. They will be over soon.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_14: Integration complete. The primary circuits of the <color=#FFFEC1>Civil Resistance</color> have been incorporated into the structure of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hive</color>. The operation may be considered successful. We must inform you that the remaining targets will still be hostile. Issachar has severed his subnet and is holding it inside the bodies around you. These are his final remnants.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_2: Our satellite is detecting a key colnode. Signature fully confirmed. After <color=#FFFEC1>Dr. Hellstrom</color> disappeared, they didn't even try to develop the technology further. Kill him and continue the operation.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_3: Clean work. We see the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color> on the eliminated target. Take it and move on.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_4: The satellite is reconstructing the map as you move, guided by your sensory input. It has firmly locked onto the station, so we are initiating the unlock sequence for the <color=#FFFEC1>Fourth Level</color>. We will try to have it done by the time you collect all three <color=#FFFEC1>Chips</color>.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_5: If our readings are correct, the key colnode is right in front of you. He should have the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color>. Eliminate the target, retrieve the device, and move on.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_6:
The reaction confirms our psychological profile data. Faced with the loss of integration, Issachar is losing the stability of his local coordination.

I can't promise it will get easier from here. But you can give yourself credit for hitting him where it hurts.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_7: Heavy interference on this level, but our satellite is keeping a lock on the station. It seems <color=#FFFEC1>Issachar</color> has figured out why we are really here. Find the key colnode here and take his <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color>. You need to find three such devices in total.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_8: We see the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color> on the eliminated target. Take it.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.ancom_9: Confirming acquisition of all three <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color>. We are ready to finish unlocking the base's Fourth Level. Head upstairs and install the chips into the control computer of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. After that, we can intercept the signal.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.issahar_1:
The future of a great people depends on the people themselves—on their will, their energy, and their creative power.

The working people of the Solar System are the only great people. Everyone to the defense of the Network!
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.issahar_2: You think you are killing us one by one? You are not killing us, you are making us stronger. You are teaching us the final form of Unity. If the people cannot be saved by a voice, they will be saved by silence. If the will cannot be free, it will become collective.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.jane_1:
The Magnum systems confirm that the Fourth Level has been unlocked.

Boss, I've got some intel for you. AnCom unlocked someone else's base like they have guest access and a favorite mug sitting on the admin's desk in the server room. Is there something we don't know about their ties to the Civil Resistance?
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.jane_2: The counterattack is almost repelled, but that was just the first wave... Everything on Pallas that can still walk is heading your way. Hold your ground.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.jane_3: All right, I suppose this means the contract is complete. Evacuation authorized. Don't try to kill everyone. Fight your way to the exit. Right now, the only thing that matters is getting out.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.dlg.space_ancom1:
HIS Unveiled has fallen. We will not waste time on formal accusations—you know yourself how wrong you were.

For AnCom, this is not simply the loss of a spacecraft. There were people on board, along with protocols and archives so ancient you could barely imagine them. Now we are blind, and the Solar System is under threat. We can no longer afford to fight a defensive war.

You have a chance to redeem yourself. The Civil Resistance possesses a technology capable of linking minds into a single network. Until now, we had classified it as a threat. Following the fall of the Unveiled, the situation has changed. We are shutting down the Master Plan and initiating the Hive Plan. If you are ready to atone for your failures, accept the contract. The target is the Humankind's Hope Citadel on Pallas. According to our data, one of the two nodes of the Hellstrom Network is deployed there. Your task is to reach the central computer and ensure the transmission of the Network's control code sequence to us.

story.hiv_1_cold_war.objective.insert_ch: Install three Red Chips into the central computer.
story.hiv_1_cold_war.objective.reach_flo: Go up to the Fourth Level.
